messages.subject: Estimating peak RAM requirements
messages.body_plain:
Is anyone able to provide advice on how to
estimate peak RAM requirements for TMB
models -- including those that have random
effects with and without sparse structures?

This calculation must be done before fitting the
model.

Thanks,
Chris

messages.body_plain:
Hi there,

Study summary:  In my study, I asked the participants to rate how much they  attended to a vibration pattern on their body.  They used a slider to answer the question. The slider range was between [0,100] with zero indicating easily and 100 indicating very hard. The study was done with 36 participants, each rating their experience 18 times. The raw values of "Attend" is shown in figure 1.

Given that my dependent variable is inflated with zeros, I decided to use the following model to fit my data with.  Though, I am not sure if I set the parameters in bold correctly. Would you please confirm whether I did it right please?

NA_fit1 <- glmmTMB(Attend ~ Bodysite + Pattern * Strength + (1 |id), data=data1, dispformula =~0, ziformula=~1, family=poisson)

Thank you again!
P

messages.body_plain:
Hi Ben,

Thank you for the quick response.

I ran into two issues here:

1. For Attend to fit under a beta distribution, the following has to be fulfilled:  0 <Attend /100< 1. Though currently  0 <= Attend/100 <=1.
2. Even if Attend/100 first between zero and 1,  I get the following error when I construct the model:

Attend_fit1 <- glmmTMB(Attend/100 ~ Bodysite + Pattern * Strength + (1 |id) + (Bodysite|id), data=data1, dispformula =~0, ziformula=~1, family=beta_family())

Error in mkTMBStruc(formula, ziformula, dispformula, combForm, mf, fr, : ~0 dispersion not implemented for ‘beta’ family

I also found this bit of a tex on how to deal with continuous inflated with zero data (please see the attachment).

I am not an expert on this topic. Could you help me make progress, please?

Thank you again!
P

messages.body_plain:
I have one more question. Do you think with the data that looks like the attached image, I can construct the same model as the attend (with beta distribution assumption)?

Diff_PA_NA_fit2 <- glmmTMB(((Diff_PA_NA+100)/200* 35 + .5) /36 ~ Bodysite + Pattern * Strength + (1 |id), data=data1,  ziformula=~1, family=beta_family(link = "logit"))

PA stands for values of positive affect. The range of the value is [0,100].
NA stands for values of negative affect. The range of the value is [0,100]. The NA is inflated with zeros.
The idea is that PA - NA should reflect the valence of an emotion that the participants experienced when receiving the haptic vibration on their body.

Thanks again for the help!!

r-sig-mix...@r-project.org; it's off-topic here, which is for
technical discussions about specific models people are writing in TMB --
not for front-ends like glmmTMB or more general statistical questions.

- it's best if you subscribe first at
https://stat.ethz.ch/mailman/listinfo/r-sig-mixed-models
- note it's a public list (e.g., change the salutation on your message,
don't post sensitive information)
- most attachments will be stripped from list messages. If you have
images, data or very complex code, consider uploading it somewhere and
posting a public link
- try to keep your questions reasonably short and accessible to a
general audience

messages.body_plain:
Thanks Cole!

For future reference, something like this worked for me, where I have an `obj` from `MakeADFun` and a `stanfit` object called `fit`. Note that you have to specify parameter names so that you don't get the posterior `lp__` samples out.

post <- as.matrix(fit, pars = c(...))
postrep <- apply(X = post, MARGIN = 1, FUN = obj$report)

This returns a list of `report()`s, which will take some list-fu to unnest to be usable, but the samples are there.

--John

messages.subject: failure to produce sparse hessian structure
messages.subject_clean: failure to produce sparse hessian structure
messages.body_plain:
I have a model with a number of random effect configurations. At its most
complex the model has two random effects, lneps_st and lneta_stl. These
are defined using the SEPARABLE macro as follows,

nll_gmrf += SEPARABLE(AR1(phiEt), GMRF(QE, bool(options(2))))(lneps_st);
nll_gmrf += SEPARABLE(AR1(phiHl),
                      SEPARABLE(AR1(phiHt), GMRF(QH, bool(options(2)))))(lneta_stl);

Here, the Qs are defined as SparseMatrix<Type> using the Q_spde function
and the random effects are PARAMETER_ARRAY objects.

In the simplest case the model only incorporates lneps_st, which is defined as,

nll_gmrf += AR1(phiEt)(lneps_st);

It is my understanding that these specifications should produce sparse hessians.
Nevertheless, in all cases dense or relatively dense hessian structures are
produced. What are the likely reasons that are causing this to happen?

As an example, in the simplest case, the following code produces,
Matrix::image(obj$env$spHess(random = TRUE))
